title: Welsh Rarebit
subtitle: Classic British cheese sauce on toast
excerpt: Welsh rarebit is not cheese on toast: it is a thick, deeply savoury sauce of mature Cheddar melted with mustard, Worcestershire sauce, and ale, spread generously on toast and grilled until bubbling and golden.

recipe.sourceNotes: Welsh rarebit (historically 'rabbit', despite containing no rabbit) is one of the oldest and most well-known British savoury dishes, documented from at least the eighteenth century. The dish is a cooked cheese sauce made with mature Cheddar, English mustard, Worcestershire sauce, and ale or stout, bound together into a thick, spreadable paste and grilled on toast. The key distinction from cheese on toast is the sauce: the cheese is not simply melted but is cooked into a béchamel or roux-based sauce that spreads evenly and grills to a uniform bubbly finish. Buck rarebit is the name given when a poached egg is placed on top. The best version uses strong, mature Cheddar and a good bitter or stout rather than a mild beer.

content.text: The rarebit sauce should be very thick before it goes on the toast; it will loosen slightly under the grill. Use the grill, not the oven: only the grill produces the characteristic fast bubbling and charring without drying out the toast. The sauce keeps refrigerated for up to three days and can be grilled straight from cold.
Melt the butter in a small saucepan. Add the flour and cook, stirring, for 1 minute. Gradually add the ale, stirring constantly, to make a smooth sauce. Cook for 2 minutes.
Remove from the heat. Add the cheese, mustard, Worcestershire sauce, and pepper. Stir until the cheese is melted and completely smooth. Stir in the egg yolk. The mixture should be very thick.

Preheat the grill to its highest setting. Toast the bread. Spread the rarebit mixture thickly and evenly over each slice, taking it right to the edges. Place under the hot grill for 3 to 4 minutes until deeply golden and bubbling. Serve immediately.
